source: Hand-curated Nov 2026. Names and coordinates from Google Places; tags and notes editorial. Closures and seasonal facts checked against NPS notices and local reports as of Nov 10, 2026 and change often: verify with NPS (nps.gov/zion) before booking. distMi is approximate road miles from the Zion Canyon Visitor Center.

items.name: Pa'rus Trail
items.note: Flat, paved 3.5-mile riverside path from the visitor center; walkers and bikes share it, no shuttle needed.

items.name: Zion Human History Museum
items.note: Small NPS museum on the canyon road with a terrace view of the Towers of the Virgin.
items.seasonNote: NPS lists fall hours (10-5) through Nov 28; confirm winter schedule.

items.name: Weeping Rock
items.note: Short, steep paved climb to a dripping alcove and hanging gardens (shuttle stop 7). The old trail beyond it to Hidden Canyon and Observation Point stays closed.

items.name: Emerald Pools (Lower)
items.note: Easy shaded walk behind a seasonal waterfall, from Zion Lodge (shuttle stop 5). Flow is thin in dry months.

items.name: Riverside Walk & Temple of Sinawava
items.note: Paved 1-mile-each-way riverside path at the end of the canyon road (last shuttle stop) and the start of The Narrows.

items.name: The Narrows (bottom-up)
items.note: Wade the Virgin River between canyon walls. Closes when flow tops 150 cfs or on a flash-flood warning; NPS also warns against submerging your head (cyanobacteria). Rent neoprene or a drysuit in Springdale in cold months.
items.seasonNote: Cold water and short days Nov-Mar: drysuit territory. Check the USGS gauge and NPS alerts the morning of.

items.name: Angels Landing
items.note: Famous chain-assisted ridge hike (Grotto, shuttle stop 6). NPS permit via lottery is required for the chained section; Scout Lookout is the no-permit turnaround.

items.name: Red Rock Grill (Zion Lodge)
items.note: Dining room inside the park at Zion Lodge, handy between Emerald Pools and the Narrows.

items.name: Canyon Overlook Trail
items.note: 1-mile round trip to a ledge over Pine Creek Canyon; trailhead is on SR-9 just east of the tunnel, with a tiny lot. SR-9 reopened Oct 9, 2026 after a rockfall, with a temporary gravel stretch; oversize vehicles are restricted.

items.name: Checkerboard Mesa Viewpoint
items.note: Roadside pullout on the Zion-Mount Carmel Highway facing the crosshatched sandstone mesa.

items.name: Observation Point (East Mesa Trail)
items.note: About 7 miles round trip to a rim higher than Angels Landing. Reachable only from the East Mesa trailhead outside the park (the Weeping Rock route is closed); the last stretch is rough dirt, and a paid shuttle runs from Zion Ponderosa.

items.name: Lava Point Overlook (Kolob Terrace)
items.note: High-country overlook at ~7,900 ft reached by the long Kolob Terrace Road; the last couple of miles are gravel.
items.seasonNote: Kolob Terrace Road closes for snow from fall to spring; Lava Point campground closed for winter Oct 5.

items.name: Grafton Ghost Town
items.note: Restored 1860s Mormon settlement and cemetery off a dirt road near Rockville; the signed walking tour takes about an hour.

items.name: Worthington Gallery
items.note: Springdale gallery of Southwest landscape painting and sculpture.

items.name: David J. West Gallery
items.note: Local landscape-photography gallery on Zion Park Blvd.

items.name: Oscar's Cafe
items.note: Big-portion Southwest and Mexican plates on a patio. Vegetarian items are marked on the menu and vegan swaps are available.

items.name: Thai Sapa
items.note: Small Thai spot; stir-fries, curries and noodles are easy to order plant-based.

items.name: Whiptail Grill
items.note: Converted gas station with a patio; tofu or veggie burrito, salads and chips with guac.

items.name: Bit & Spur Restaurant & Saloon
items.note: Longtime Southwest-Mexican saloon; vegetarian, vegan and dairy-free dishes are labeled on the menu.

items.name: Spotted Dog Cafe
items.note: Restaurant and bar at Flanigan's Inn with a few vegan options.

items.name: Zion Canyon Brew Pub
items.note: Brewpub next to the park entrance; lists some vegetarian and vegan dishes.

items.name: MeMe's Cafe
items.note: Breakfast all day and lunch; vegan options are limited (oatmeal, a house vegan meatloaf, sandwich swaps).

items.name: Wild Thyme Bistro at Trees Ranch
items.note: Garden-fed bistro on the edge of town; menu marks vegetarian (VG) and vegan (V) dishes such as black bean sliders and yellow curry.

items.name: FeelLove Coffee (Springdale)
items.note: Coffee, breakfast and brunch; Google lists it as a vegan and vegetarian restaurant.

items.name: Bonrue Bakery
items.note: Bakery and donut counter on Zion Park Blvd.

items.name: Kolob Canyons Scenic Drive
items.note: 5-mile paved road to Kolob Canyons Viewpoint off I-15 exit 40, up to ~1,000 ft under red fins. Closes in winter for snow or ice, and walking the road is not allowed during plowing.

items.name: Timber Creek Overlook Trail
items.note: About 1 mile round trip with little climbing to a panorama of Kolob Canyons, the Pine Valley Mountains and Kolob Terrace; good for little legs.

items.name: Cedar Breaks National Monument (Point Supreme)
items.note: Red-rock amphitheater above 10,000 ft with a 5-mile road of overlooks and wildflower meadows.
items.seasonNote: UT-148 is closed by snow outside roughly late May to October.

items.name: Utah Shakespeare Festival
items.note: Repertory theater with a free Greenshow before evening performances.
items.seasonNote: Summer and fall seasons only; check the schedule for dates.

items.name: Parowan Gap Petroglyphs
items.note: Ancient rock-art panels in a wind gap north of Cedar City; open 24 hours, no fee.

items.name: Namaste America Indian Cuisine
items.note: Indian restaurant that Google lists as vegetarian and vegan friendly.

items.name: Centro Woodfired Pizzeria
items.note: Woodfired pizza and Italian on Center Street, two blocks from the Shakespeare Festival.

items.name: Snow Canyon State Park
items.note: Red and white Navajo sandstone against black lava; easy picks are Jenny's Canyon, the lava tubes and the Petrified Dunes. Enter from the south end for the best drive.

items.name: Tuacahn Amphitheatre
items.note: Broadway-style musicals in an open-air theater inside a red-rock canyon near Ivins.
items.seasonNote: Main shows run roughly spring through fall; check the schedule.

items.name: Quail Creek State Park
items.note: Warm reservoir near Hurricane with paddling and rentals; free life jackets are available.

items.name: The Hearty Beet Cafe
items.note: Cafe listed as vegan and vegetarian in St. George.

items.name: Cafe FeelLove (St. George)
items.note: Downtown brunch cafe listed as vegan and vegetarian.

items.name: Mint Indian Bistro
items.note: North Indian restaurant that Google lists as vegetarian and vegan friendly.

items.name: Mixed Greens
items.note: Salad, acai and juice counter for a quick lunch.

items.name: Best Friends Animal Sanctuary
items.note: Largest no-kill animal sanctuary in Angel Canyon; free tours, a welcome center and views. Reviewers mention a free 90-minute guided tour.

items.name: Coral Pink Sand Dunes State Park
items.note: Coral-colored dunes with sandboard rentals; a state-park fee applies and national park passes are not accepted.

items.name: Peekaboo Canyon Wood Fired Kitchen
items.note: Kanab's all-vegetarian-and-vegan restaurant: wood-fired pizza plus Impossible and Beyond dishes. Closed Mondays.

items.name: Angel Village Cafe
items.note: Plant-based buffet lunch at Best Friends, served 11:30 to 1 daily.

items.name: Rocking V Cafe
items.note: Art-filled eatery in an 1892 mercantile; slow food from meats to vegan plates.

items.name: Wild Thyme Cafe (Kanab)
items.note: Beef, fish and chicken plus ample vegan and vegetarian selections.

items.name: Horseshoe Bend Overlook
items.note: Short walk to the rim above the Colorado River's horseshoe meander. Long day trip: roughly 2.5 hours from Zion each way.

items.name: Lower Antelope Canyon (guided tour)
items.note: Navajo-guided slot canyon tours; booking is required and tours cancel for flash-flood risk.
